newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rangebound, seen staying weak.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rangebound, seen staying weak.

text.p: * Ringgit rangebound with position squaring limiting dollar's rise
* Dollar well bid by offshore players
* Dollar sentiment helped by strength against majors
The ringgit was rangebound in early Asian trading on Monday but was expected to maintain its weakness against the dollar, dealers said.
"There's nothing much happening this morning. Trading volume is very thin," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
"Some players are still squaring out positions but the dollar remains well bid," he said.
Dealers said they expected the ringgit to remain weak on the back of the dollar's strength against major currencies.
"We are still looking at ringgit trading below 2.65. Given the thin volume, 20 (million) dollars is enough to move dollar/ringgit," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
An Asian central bankers meeting in Shanghai on Friday provided no surprises.
At the meeting, Southeast Asian central banks signed an agreement to renew a currency swap accord, providing short-term liquidity financing to ease temporary balance of payment needs.
At 0215 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6500/10 to a dollar. It closed at 2.6480/10 in Kuala Lumpur on Friday.
